name: application-notification-preferences-grid
title: Notification Preferences Grid
description: Channel-by-event notification matrix of checkboxes (Email/Push/SMS) with per-cell disabled/required states, driven by a typed channels/rows prop contract.
useWhen: A settings page needs users to configure which channel (email, push, SMS) delivers each type of notification.
Some notification/channel combinations must be locked (e.g. security alerts always email) while others stay optional.
The event list and channel list are both data-driven and may grow independently.
avoidWhen: There is only one channel — a simple checkbox list per event is simpler than a matrix.
Users need granular per-recipient rules, not per-event-type rules — a rules/filter builder fits better.
The number of events is very large — paginate or group events instead of one long matrix.
responsiveBehavior: The table scrolls horizontally within its own container on narrow viewports where the channel columns no longer fit; the event label column should remain legible at any width.
accessibility: Each checkbox carries a composed aria-label naming both the event and the channel, since the grid layout alone doesn't convey that pairing to screen readers.
Disabled cells (unavailable or required-and-locked) use the native disabled attribute plus a footnote explaining why, not just a dimmed appearance.
Column headers use scope='col' so assistive technology associates each checkbox column with its channel label.

variants.title: Notification Preferences Grid
variants.description: Event-by-channel checkbox matrix with a required always-on cell, an unavailable disabled cell, and a footnote explaining the locked row.
accessibility: The required Security alerts / Email cell is disabled-checked with an aria-label noting it is required, and a footnote explains why.

variants.title: Notification Preferences Grid (Dark)
variants.description: Notification matrix adapted for dark surfaces with the same channel-header, checkbox-cell, and footnote structure.
accessibility: Checkbox borders, disabled-state dimming, and footnote text must meet WCAG AA contrast on dark surfaces.
